title: Promise Basics
Promise Rejection
code:
const p = Promise.reject(new Error('oops'));
p.catch(err => console.log(err.message));

title: Unhandled Promise Rejection
code:
const p = new Promise((_, reject) => reject('error'));
console.log('done');

bugs.explanation: An unhandled Promise rejection causes `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning` in Node.js and an error event in browsers. Always attach a `.catch()` handler or use `try/catch` with `async/await`.

title: async/await Basic
await in Non-async Function

bugs.explanation: `await` can only be used inside an `async` function (or at the top level of a module). Using it in a regular function causes `SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions`. Mark the function with `async`.

Fetch API
code:
fetch('/api/users')
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data))
  .catch(err => console.error(err));

title: Fetch Not Rejecting on 4xx

bugs.explanation: `fetch` only rejects the Promise on network errors, not HTTP error status codes (4xx/5xx). A 404 or 500 response is resolved, not rejected. Always check `res.ok` (or `res.status`) and throw explicitly on error responses.
